summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of aggressive mesenteric fibromatosis, recurrent small bowel obstructions, and chronic TPN via a femoral catheter was admitted two days after a prior discharge due to a low-grade fever of 100.5°F noted at home. She had mild erythema at the femoral line site and ongoing nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Labs showed elevated creatinine (1.2) and leukocytosis (WBC 10.4), which improved with IV fluids and supportive care. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth. She remained afebrile throughout the hospitalization. The line site showed no signs of active infection, and pain during infusions was attributed to possible irritation or residual inflammation. She was discharged home after 48 hours of observation with stable vital signs, normalizing labs, and no infectious source identified. Outpatient follow-up was arranged for repeat line evaluation. Chronic conditions, including anemia, hypothyroidism, and migraines, remained stable.
